caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION:The figure presents a bar chart illustrating the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars representing standard deviation. The horizontal axis categorizes data by language family, displaying labels IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," ranges from 0 to 30 with linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 5. Six data series are compared: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (blue), mBERT-R2 (red), XLM-R2 (dark red), mBERT-B2 (green), and XLM-B2 (dark green). Each language family has a bar for each model configuration, with error bars extending above and below the bar tops. The shortest bars across all configurations are consistently found in the Uralic and Isolate families, generally below 5, while the IE-Indic family exhibits the tallest bars, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25. The bars are not sorted in any particular order. No bars are visually emphasized beyond the standard error bar representation.
